PythonExport.Name: MaterialListPy

Documentation.UserDocu:
A list of materials, which behaves like a list of App.Material.
Read from a view provider it is a LIVE VIEW of that appearance: writing to it -- vp.ShapeAppearance[0].DiffuseColor = c, or one of the indexed setters below -- changes the object, records an undo step and redraws.
Assigning it anywhere else DETACHES it into a plain value. A detached list shares its storage with the one it came from until either side writes, so copying one costs nothing and mutating one never surprises the other:
a = vp.ShapeAppearance # a live view of the appearance a[0].DiffuseColor = (1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0) # changes the object
b = App.MaterialList(vp.ShapeAppearance) # a value, shares storage b[0] = mat # changes b alone vp.ShapeAppearance = b # and this is what changes the object
Indexing yields a copy of the entry with a link back, so writing a field on it writes the whole entry back to that index. The per field setters below take Index=-1 to mean every entry.
append(Material) -> None: add one entry at the end.
extend(iterable) -> None: add every material of an iterable.
insert(index, Material) -> None: insert one entry before index.

copy() -> MaterialList: a detached copy.
It shares this list's storage until one of them is written to, so it costs a pointer however long the list is.

detach() -> None: stop being a view of the object.
The list keeps the value it has and writing to it stops changing anything else. Assigning the list to a property does this too.

setSize(count, [Material]) -> None: resize the list.
Entries added take the given material, or -- with none given -- what an unset entry of this list reads as.
getMaterial(index) -> Material: one entry, as a copy.

setMaterial(index, Material) -> None: write one whole entry.
Index=-1 writes every entry.
How many entries the list has; the same as len().
Whether writing to this list writes to the object it came from.

Whether the stored values are read as PBR quantities.
One flag for the whole list. Setting it reinterprets the values; it converts nothing (App.Material.PBR does convert).
